## Purpose

This procedure describes the safe operation of gravity convection and
forced-air drying ovens used in the EA Program laboratory. Drying ovens
are used to determine gravimetric moisture content of soil, sediment,
and plant tissue samples (see
[SOP-L400 Soil Moisture](SOP-L400-soil-moisture.qmd)), to pre-dry
samples before loss on ignition (see
[SOP-L406 Loss on Ignition](SOP-L406-loss-on-ignition.qmd)), to dry
glassware, and to regenerate desiccants. Consistent oven operation
ensures accurate and reproducible mass-loss measurements across the
laboratory [@gardner1986; @robertson1999].


## Scope

- **Applies to:** All gravity convection and forced-air drying ovens in
  the EA Program laboratory, operated at temperatures up to 250 C
- **Does not apply to:** Muffle furnaces (550+ C; see SOP-L50), vacuum
  ovens, microwave drying, or autoclaves
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve SOP, ensure training compliance     |
| Lab Manager       | Maintain ovens, schedule annual calibration checks |
| Trained Personnel | Operate ovens following this SOP, report malfunctions |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Oven surfaces and contents reach temperatures up to
  250 C. Severe burns can result from touching hot surfaces, shelves,
  or sample containers without proper PPE. Steam may escape when
  opening the door if drying wet samples.
- **Chemical:** Do not dry samples containing volatile organic solvents,
  flammable materials, or corrosive chemicals in these ovens. Drying
  ovens are not explosion-proof. Volatile fumes can accumulate inside
  the oven chamber and pose fire or explosion risks.
- **Electrical:** Do not operate ovens with damaged power cords or
  plugs. Ensure the oven is properly grounded.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Heat-resistant gloves or oven mitts (required when loading/unloading)
- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Closed-toed shoes

### Emergency Procedures

For burns, cool the affected area under cool running water for at least
10 minutes. Seek medical attention for burns with blistering. If smoke
or unusual odors are detected, turn off the oven, unplug it, and
ventilate the area. Refer to
[SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd).

## Procedure

### Pre-Use Checks

1. Verify the oven is clean and free of residue from previous use
2. Check that the oven vent is unobstructed (gravity convection ovens
   rely on passive airflow; blocked vents cause uneven heating)
3. Confirm the temperature setpoint using the oven's built-in display
   or controller
4. Verify the temperature against an independent thermometer or
   thermocouple placed inside the oven. The reading should agree within
   +/- 2 C of the setpoint. If it does not, contact the lab manager.

### Setting the Temperature

Common drying temperatures used in the EA Program laboratory:

| Application                     | Temperature | Duration         | Reference SOP |
|:--------------------------------|:------------|:-----------------|:--------------|
| Gravimetric soil moisture       | 105 C       | 24+ hours        | SOP-L41       |
| Pre-drying soil for LOI         | 105 C       | 24+ hours        | SOP-L50       |
| Drying glassware                | 105 C       | 2--4 hours       | --            |
| Drying plant tissue             | 65--70 C    | 48--72 hours     | --            |
| Regenerating Drierite desiccant | 210 C       | 1--2 hours       | --            |
| Acid-treated soil (IC removal)  | 105 C       | Until dry        | SOP-L51       |

1. Set the temperature using the oven controller dial or digital
   display
2. Allow the oven to reach the target temperature and stabilize before
   loading samples (typically 30--60 minutes)
3. Record the setpoint and actual temperature in your lab notebook

### Loading Samples

1. Arrange samples on oven shelves with adequate spacing to allow air
   circulation. Do not stack containers or block vents.
2. Place containers with the lids removed or loosely resting to allow
   moisture to escape
3. For large batches, distribute samples evenly across shelves to
   minimize temperature gradients
4. Close the oven door promptly after loading

::: {.callout-tip}
### Tip
Place a small label or sign on the oven door indicating: your name,
the setpoint temperature, the date and time samples were loaded, and
the expected removal time. This prevents others from accidentally
changing the temperature or disturbing your samples.
:::

### Monitoring

1. Check the oven temperature at the start and end of each drying cycle
   using the independent thermometer
2. Do not open the oven door unnecessarily during drying, as this
   introduces cool air and extends drying time
3. For multi-day drying, check the oven temperature at least once daily

### Removing Samples

1. Wear heat-resistant gloves or oven mitts
2. Use metal tongs for small containers (aluminum tins, crucibles)
3. Transfer hot containers directly into a desiccator to cool to room
   temperature. Do not weigh hot samples; thermal convection currents
   around hot objects cause unstable balance readings [@harris2020].
4. Allow samples to cool in the desiccator for 20--30 minutes before
   weighing
5. Close the oven door after removing samples

### Verifying Dryness (Constant Mass)

For analytical applications (soil moisture, LOI), drying is complete
only when the sample reaches constant mass:

1. After the initial drying period, remove the sample, cool in the
   desiccator, and weigh
2. Return the sample to the oven for an additional 2--4 hours
3. Cool and re-weigh
4. If the mass has changed by less than 0.01 g between successive
   weighings, constant mass has been achieved
5. If the mass has decreased by more than 0.01 g, return to the oven
   and repeat until constant mass is reached

### Shutdown

1. If the oven will not be used for several days, turn it off using the
   power switch or controller
2. Leave the door slightly ajar to prevent moisture buildup and odors
   inside the chamber
3. Ensure no samples remain in the oven before shutting down


## Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

- Verify oven temperature against an independent thermometer at least
  monthly; record in the oven calibration log
- Acceptable temperature accuracy: +/- 2 C of setpoint at 105 C
- If the oven temperature drifts beyond +/- 5 C, remove the oven from
  service and contact the lab manager
- Ensure the desiccator contains active (indicating) desiccant;
  regenerate or replace when the indicator changes color
- For analytical drying, always confirm constant mass (Section 6.6)
  rather than relying on a fixed drying time alone

### Interferences

- Overcrowding the oven can create temperature gradients and uneven
  drying, leading to inconsistent results
- Opening the oven door frequently extends drying time and introduces
  moisture
- Drying samples containing volatile compounds at 105 C will cause mass
  loss beyond water content, biasing moisture determinations


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type              | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Dried soil samples      | Standard trash or return to field site   |
| Aluminum tins           | Clean and reuse, or recycle              |
| Spent desiccant         | Regenerate at 210 C or dispose as non-hazardous solid waste |

## Training Record

Before using the drying oven independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP and [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   in full
2. Demonstrate proper use of heat-resistant gloves and tongs
3. Demonstrate setting the oven temperature and verifying it with an
   independent thermometer
4. Demonstrate loading and unloading samples, including transfer to the
   desiccator
5. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager


## Appendix A: Troubleshooting {.appendix}

| Symptom                          | Probable Cause                     | Corrective Action                          |
|:---------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------|
| Oven does not heat               | Power switch off, unplugged, or blown fuse | Check power connections; replace fuse if needed |
| Temperature overshoots setpoint  | Faulty thermostat or controller    | Remove from service; contact lab manager   |
| Uneven drying across samples     | Overcrowded shelves or blocked vent | Redistribute samples; check vent is clear  |
| Samples not reaching constant mass after 48 hours | Very wet or clay-rich samples; temperature too low | Verify setpoint is 105 C; extend drying time; check oven seal |
| Unusual odor during drying       | Contaminated samples or residue from previous use | Turn off oven; ventilate; clean interior   |
